name: Badr al-Dīn Abū Muḥammad Maḥmūd ibn Aḥmad al-ʿAynī
summary: Ḥanafī scholar of Turkish origin in Mamluk Cairo, commentator on al-Bukhārī, who explained the verses quoted as evidence in the commentaries on the Alfiyya and wrote on Marāḥ al-arwāḥ.
bio: Al-ʿAynī was born in ʿAyntāb in 762/1361 and came to Cairo, where he was market inspector, judge and a familiar of the Mamluk sultans; his ʿUmdat al-qārī on al-Bukhārī is one of the great commentaries of hadith.

In grammar his al-Maqāṣid al-naḥwiyya, known as al-Shawāhid al-kubrā, explains every verse of poetry that the four commentaries on the Alfiyya quote as evidence: who said it, what it means and where its point lies; it is printed in the margin of the Alfiyya's commentaries. In ṣarf he commented on Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Masʿūd's Marāḥ al-arwāḥ (Malāḥ al-alwāḥ). He died in Cairo in 855/1451.

works.title: Malāḥ al-alwāḥ fī sharḥ Marāḥ al-arwāḥ
